tail:
The Step-6 routing repair is on disk. In [tools/step6-scope.mjs](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/tools/step6-scope.mjs), I fixed the mechanical gate mismatch so `adjudicate` accepts the same frozen reader batch label that `split` already routed, and I limited `ledger-unowned` to decision-eligible Step-6 subjects instead of forcing the global contract-audit summary rows through fake item decisions. I also retagged the stale touched decisions in [research/frontier-19-alpha-b-6b-decisions.json](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/frontier-19-alpha-b-6b-decisions.json) and [research/frontier-19-alpha-d-6b-decisions.json](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/frontier-19-alpha-d-6b-decisions.json) from `accepted_repair` to `amended_repair` where the final carrier had later changed, and recorded that in the matching group reports [research/frontier-19-alpha-b-6b.md](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/frontier-19-alpha-b-6b.md) and [research/frontier-19-alpha-d-6b.md](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/frontier-19-alpha-d-6b.md). I also updated the reader brief/schema and [ARCHITECTURE.md](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/ARCHITECTURE.md) to reflect the gate behavior.

Verification is green on the live run: `node tools/step6-scope.mjs check --run frontier-19 --phase adjudicate` now returns `step6-scope: 443 item(s) routed, 99 adjudication obligation(s), 0 error(s)`. I also checked the affected batches individually; the only red seen in isolated batch-1/4 runs was the expected batch-filter artifact around batch-10 published-repair ownership, while the full run is clean. I could not use `tools/autopilot/test/step6-routing.test.mts` as a reliable regression signal here because that fixture already fails in this sandbox on `spawnSync cp EPERM`, and it also has an unrelated pre-existing frontier-18 assertion failure.
